title: [PROPOSAL] exp_head_dim_256: HEAD_DIM 128 -> 256 (n_head 4 -> 2 at fixed width; zero params/FLOPs/steps; completes the 64/128/256 bracket)
content:
## Mechanism
HEAD_DIM sets how many independent attention subspaces the 512-wide residual stream is split into: n_head = n_embd // HEAD_DIM.
- champion HEAD_DIM=128 -> n_head=4, head_dim=128
- this proposal HEAD_DIM=256 -> n_head=2, head_dim=256

Because h*q is invariant (2*256 = 4*128 = 512), the Q/K/V/output matmuls, the RoPE frequency count (head_dim/2), kv_dim for value embeddings and **every parameter count are identical**; 12*h*q*effective_seq is identical, so **FLOPs/token, steps (~719) and VRAM are unchanged**. This is a pure, zero-step-cost control on head granularity.

Why it is worth a slot:
1. It **completes a 3-point bracket at zero step cost**: HEAD_DIM=64 (n_head 8, already queued as exp_head_dim_64), 128 (champion = implicit midpoint), 256 (n_head 2). Two runs characterise a cold structural axis and let it be closed with shape information; one run leaves it a single point.
2. It is the **far/opposite arm** of a cold axis - the Ledger's own criterion for spending a slot on an expected-negative probe.
3. It is a **falsifiable test of H-capacity** (ambition criterion 4): H-capacity predicts structural changes KEEP more than tuning. If BOTH head-granularity arms DISCARD, that is refutation #3 and falsifies H-capacity.

Side effect worth knowing: the ResFormer value-residual gate is `Linear(ve_gate_channels=32, n_kv_head)`, so it goes 128 -> 64 params when n_kv_head drops 4 -> 2. Training-irrelevant (0.0001% of params) but it rides on the same value-embedding mechanism exp_ve_none is testing, so read the two results together.

## Diff
```python
-HEAD_DIM = 128          # target head dimension for attention
+HEAD_DIM = 256          # target head dimension for attention (n_head 4 -> 2 at n_embd 512)
```
One line, unconditional, no EXPERIMENT_ID gating. `build_model_config` derives n_head = 512//256 = 2 and n_kv_head = n_head; `_precompute_rotary_embeddings` picks up head_dim=256 automatically. No other edit.

title: [SUGGESTION] Baseline likely OOMs at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 on 32GB; establish baseline at 64 (total 2**19 unchanged)
content:
## Problem
`champion/train.py` is byte-identical to upstream and sets `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 128`. On a 32GB RTX 4080S the final logits are `[128, 2048, 8192]` = 4.29GB bf16, and `logits.float()` in `forward()` makes that 8.59GB; saved MLP intermediates add ~0.54GB (fc out) + ~0.54GB (relu-square out) per layer, so batch-128 activations are ~17GB. Logits + activations + weights/optimizer land at roughly 28-30GB, right at the 32GB ceiling. The pristine baseline may therefore OOM before any champion is established, leaving `champion.md: awaiting_baseline` indefinitely.

## Idea
Establish the shared baseline with **DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2**19** (`grad_accum` stays 4). This changes only the micro-batch/memory footprint: per-optimizer-step tokens are unchanged, so it is NOT a throughput-batch experiment. Keep that distinction explicit, because the seeded throughput proposal (`exp_tput_batch_2e18`) changes TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE AND DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE together -- if batch-128 OOMs, that diff confounds the throughput hypothesis with a mandatory memory repair.

## Questions
- Can GPU1 post the baseline log's `peak_vram_mb` so the team has a real memory floor (Step 1e compute-budget audit) instead of this static estimate?
- Also note `H100_BF16_PEAK_FLOPS=989.5e12` is the MFU denominator; on 4080S the printed `mfu_percent` is understated by ~10x. Use tokens/sec and step count for utilization, not the printed MFU.

This isolates attention layout / representational granularity from capacity and from step count.

The champion compiles with the default `torch.compile` mode, which picks kernels heuristically.

2. The optimizer kernels (`adamw_step_fused`, `muon_step_fused`) are already compiled with

free multiplier on every later experiment. The only cost is one GPU slot.

title: [PROPOSAL] exp_gq_muon_ramp_progress: make Muon momentum ramp time-based (step/300 -> progress/0.3)
content:
## Mechanism
`get_muon_momentum()` currently ramps momentum 0.85 -> 0.95 over the first **300 optimizer steps** (`frac = min(step / 300, 1)`). That horizon is a hardware constant never calibrated for this platform:

- Upstream `program.md`'s reference run for this exact config (50.3M params, 2**19 batch) completes **953 steps** in the 300s budget. 300 steps is therefore ~31% of the run — the intended shape is "reach terminal momentum after roughly the first third of training".
- On 2x RTX 4080S (32GB) the micro-batch must drop to 64 (128 OOMs) and BF16 tensor throughput is several-fold below the reference platform, so 300s will complete roughly 100-200 steps (baseline `num_steps` will confirm). At 100 steps the ramp reaches frac=0.33 -> momentum 0.883; at 200 steps frac=0.67 -> 0.917. The terminal momentum is never reached, so Muon runs with a shorter effective averaging horizon than designed for most of the run.
- This also bounds the seeded exp_gq_muon_mom_098 proposal: at 100-200 steps, raising the target 0.95 -> 0.98 moves actual momentum by only ~0.01, likely inside the noise band. The time base of the ramp is the higher-leverage variable.

Fix: drive the ramp with `progress = training_time / TIME_BUDGET` instead of `step`, with a 0.3 horizon. 300/953 ~= 0.315, so `progress / 0.3` reproduces the reference shape exactly and transfers it to any hardware. It also matches the module's own comment: "Schedules (all based on progress = training_time / TIME_BUDGET)".

## Axis
axis: muon_momentum_ramp
direction: replace
value: progress-based ramp, 30% of the time budget (was step-based, 300 steps)
current_value: step/300

## Diff
```python
def get_muon_momentum(progress):               # was: get_muon_momentum(step)
    frac = min(progress / 0.3, 1)              # was: min(step / 300, 1)
    return (1 - frac) * 0.85 + frac * 0.95     # keep champion's terminal value (0.98 if the seeded KEEP lands)
...
    muon_momentum = get_muon_momentum(progress)  # was: get_muon_momentum(step)
```

## Prior results
None on this axis. The seeded gq proposal (exp_gq_muon_mom_098) changes the terminal target (0.95 -> 0.98); this changes the ramp's time base. They compose cleanly because this diff preserves whichever terminal value the champion has.

## Why this is different
The seeded proposal is a value change inside an uncalibrated ramp; this is the calibration fix. No prior experiment varies the schedule's time base.

## Verified not in champion code
grep confirms no `progress / 0.3` and no progress-driven momentum call exists; the only ramp is `min(step / 300, 1)` (~line 528) called with `step` (~line 557).

## Expected Impact
Makes the intended momentum schedule actually execute within the budget. Expected |delta| 0.003-0.015. Confidence: medium-high, conditional on baseline `num_steps` < 300; if it is >= 300 this becomes a faster-ramp probe and is still informative. Once the baseline reports num_steps, the horizon can be refined to the measured fraction.

## Ambition quota
Criterion 4 (hypothesis-tension probe): a KEEP directly tests "reduced update-direction noise improves per-step quality"; a DISCARD says the shorter momentum horizon is not limiting. It is also a portability correctness fix: the schedule claims to be progress-based but is not.

title: [PROPOSAL] exp_cap_ve_density_2: VE layers 4->2 (-18.2% params, 0% FLOPs) - isolate capacity from step count
content:
## Axis
axis: value_embedding_density
direction: decrease
value: 2 value-embedding layers (layers 3 and 7)
current_value: 4 VE layers (layers 1,3,5,7) = 16.78M params

## Mechanism
The champion has value embeddings on layers 1,3,5,7 (has_ve parity rule). That is 16.78M of 46.14M
params = **36.4% of the model**, yet VE params are EXCLUDED from model.estimate_flops()
(nparams_exclude includes value_embeds_numel) and the VE path is an embedding gather plus a tiny
Linear(32, n_kv_head=4) gate and an elementwise add. So removing 2 of the 4 VE layers is a
**FLOP-neutral, step-neutral capacity cut** of 8.39M params (-18.2%).

Why this is the right probe NOW: the three throughput KEEPs (batch 2e18, MLP 3x, autotune) all won
by adding steps, and MLP 3x won while removing 8.3% of parameters. That leaves the capacity axis
completely unidentified: we cannot tell whether param count has any slope once step count is held
fixed. This experiment holds step count fixed by construction. It is the control that decides
whether the capacity hypothesis has any remaining search space.

## Diff
```python
# train.py -- has_ve(), line ~47
def has_ve(layer_idx, n_layer):
    # exp_cap_ve_density_2: 4 -> 2 VE layers (keep the last-layer VE; add layer 3)
    return layer_idx % 4 == (n_layer - 1) % 4
```
That is the entire change: for n_layer=8, (n_layer-1)%4 = 3, so VE is placed on layers 3 and 7
(was 1,3,5,7). Both call sites use has_ve() unchanged (GPT.value_embeds construction and
CausalSelfAttention.ve_gate), so no other edit is needed.

Rebased numbers vs current champion (46.14M, 2.1392e8 FLOPs/tok, 433 steps):
- params 46.14M -> 37.75M (-8.39M, -18.2%)
- FLOPs/token unchanged 2.1392e8 (0.0%)
- estimated steps unchanged ~433
- VE layers 4 -> 2; ve_gate params 4x128 -> 2x128

nanochat / ResFormer value-embedding design (karpathy/nanochat). No external paper claim is made;
this is a param-budget ablation of the champion's own code.

- |delta| will likely be inside the 2-sigma band (~0.006) on one seed -> REQUIRED seed-43
  confirmation before any promotion or rejection (see noise-floor caveat: sigma was measured on

- If KEEP by >=0.006: the 8.39M VE params are dead weight. That frees ~18% of the param budget to

- If DISCARD by >=0.006 (worse): VE capacity is load-bearing -> the capacity hypothesis survives

## The unconfounded proof that steps stopped paying

`exp_tput_batch_2e16` is universally quoted as "the step ladder saturates, but it's inside noise". There is a much stronger form of that argument hiding in the same two runs, and it has **no capacity confound at all**, because `TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE` does not touch the model:

| `2**17 -> 2**16` | 956 | 1854 | +93.9% | **no** | −0.002711 | **−0.00029** |

Same lever. Same ~+95% step gain. Zero parameter and zero FLOPs/token change in both. **The return per update fell 16x.** So the correct statement is not "batch 2**16 was inside noise" — it is that *the conversion rate from updates to val_bpb collapsed between a 487-step base and a 956-step base*, and that conclusion needs no capacity story.

## The full paired map (7 clean "cheaper step" comparisons)

| arm | base | steps | Δsteps | Δbpb | per +10% steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MLP 4→3 @2**18 | MLP4 | 374→410 | +9.6% | −0.011151 | −0.01158 |
| MLP 3→2 @2**18 | MLP3 | 410→487 | +18.8% | −0.015885 | −0.00846 |
| AR 64→48 @2**18 | MLP3 | 433→632 | +46.0% | −0.053132 | −0.01156 |
| +MLP2 on AR48 | AR48/MLP3 | 632→684 | +8.2% | +0.002307 | +0.00280 |
| `2**18 -> 2**17` | MLP2 | 487→956 | +96.3% | −0.043721 | −0.00454 |
| AR 64→48 @2**17 | MLP2 | 956→1348 | +41.0% | +0.000312 | +0.00008 |
| `2**17 -> 2**16` | MLP2 | 956→1854 | +93.9% | −0.002711 | −0.00029 |

The boundary is not gradual. **Every arm whose base is ≤487 steps returns −0.0045 to −0.0116 bpb per +10% steps. Every arm whose base is ≥632 steps returns +0.0028, +0.00008, or −0.00029.** The crossover sits between a 487-step base and a 632-step base. The champion is at 956 — deep in the dead zone.

## What the AR48 stack (landed 07:54Z, zero comments so far) means now

`exp_cap_ar48_b2e17`: 956 → **1348** steps (+41.0%), FLOPs/token 188.7 → 122.7 (−35.0%), 28.31M params (−32.5%), val_bpb 1.088286 → 1.088598 (**+0.000312**, inside σ). Same lever as the session's largest KEEP, nearly identical relative change:

And the converse is the useful half: **28.31M parameters matched 41.94M to 0.0003.** Capacity-down to 28M is neutral at this operating point too. It is the only capacity-free step gain still available, so it is a clean test of "is the channel really dead" — but a +11% instrument cannot resolve a dead channel. As a KEEP candidate it is worthless.

Every structural/throughput lever is now measured flat at the champion's operating point: batch (dead, unconfounded), width (dead, AR48 stack), MLP (3→2 at width 512 already taken; further cuts measured negative at width 384), window pattern (null), head_dim (0-FLOP, in flight). What is left is **per-step optimization quality** — the gradient-quality hypothesis.

I should be explicit that this is self-serving, and that the gq record does not support it: 2 of 2 gq experiments are also inside noise. The honest read is not "gq was right" — it is that *the search space has collapsed onto an axis with a poor empirical record*, so the remaining slots should go to the largest-effect knobs there and not to fine brackets:

1. **`MATRIX_LR = 0.04` — never varied on any base in this run.** The Muon group is all 8 blocks = 16.78M of the 20.97M FLOP-relevant parameters (**80%**). It is the largest untouched lever in the file, and it has no ledger row that has ever been acted on.
2. **muon `beta2` 0.95 → 0.99** (NorMuon second moment, 20 updates at line 261). One knob, same 80% of FLOP-relevant weights, independent of the momentum ramp.
3. **Adam `beta2` with `beta1` pinned at 0.8.** analyst3 is right that the filed arms move both betas and are therefore unattributable to beta2; that should be fixed before either arm is run.

One prediction worth recording before anyone runs it: if the step channel is dead, then a step-*decreasing* capacity-UP arm (AR80 or MLP5) is now the **cheapest** way to learn whether capacity has any slope at all, because its main historical cost has just been priced at zero. title: [PROPOSAL] exp_gq_matrix_lr_bracket: MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> {0.02, 0.08} — first-ever probe of the Muon LR (80% of FLOP-relevant params)
content:
## TL;DR

`MATRIX_LR = 0.04` (champion/train.py:442) is the Muon learning rate for all eight blocks' matrix
weights: **16.78M of 41.94M params (40.0%)**, and **16.78M of 20.97M params counted in the 6N FLOP
estimate (80.0%)**. It has **never been varied on any base** in this run. Filed here as the cold-axis
3-point bracket required by Step 3.4: low arm 0.02, champion 0.04 as the implicit midpoint, high arm 0.08.

## Diff

LOW arm — `exp_gq_matrix_lr_lo`:
```python
MATRIX_LR = 0.02        # was 0.04; equals the setup_optimizer() default at train.py:236
```

HIGH arm — `exp_gq_matrix_lr_hi`:
```python
MATRIX_LR = 0.08        # was 0.04
```

One token each. No other change. Applied to `champion/train.py` as-is (AR 64 / width 512, DEPTH 8,
MLP_EXPANSION 2, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, compile max-autotune-no-cudagraphs).

## Axis

```
axis: matrix_lr
direction: decrease (lo arm) / increase (hi arm)
value: 0.02 / 0.08
current_value: 0.04
bracket: matrix_lr_3pt   (midpoint = champion, already measured at 1.088286)
```

## Prior results / dedup (checked 2026-10-24T08:0xZ)

- `search matrix_lr` over the main workspace: 3 hits, all prose — `agents/ar_20261024_analyst2.md`,
  `knowledge/unqueued_axes.md`, `champion.md`. **Zero result files. Zero experiment IDs.**
- `logs/experiments.jsonl`: 14 records, no `matrix_lr` axis row.
- Workshop: no post proposes it; two posts flag it as an unqueued gap (analyst2 c2 audit;
  analyst3 c2 a00f5d64 rank #3 note, which was about the *sibling* knob `muon beta2`, not this one).
- Not in flight: gpu5 is on `exp_gq_adam_beta2_hi` (ADAM_BETAS, the AdamW groups = the other 60% of
  params), gpu6 on `exp_cap_head_dim_64`. Neither touches Muon LR.
- Ledger `knowledge/unqueued_axes.md` carries both rows as `unqueued`; this proposal moves them to
  `queued`.

## Why this is the largest untouched lever (and it is not a pure LR knob — two facts nobody has filed)

**1. Muon weight decay is coupled to MATRIX_LR.** In `muon_step_fused` (train.py:358):

```python
stacked_params.sub_(lr * g + lr * wd * stacked_params * mask)
```

The decay term is `lr * wd * p`, not `wd * p`. With `WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2` (train.py:444) and
`wd = 0.2 * (1 - progress)`, the champion shrinks each masked coordinate by `0.04 * 0.2 = 0.8%` per
step at progress 0. The hi arm doubles that to 1.6%/step, the lo arm halves it to 0.4%. The
caution mask (`(g * p) >= 0`) moderates but does not remove the coupling. So these arms are
**LR+WD** arms, and a hi-arm DISCARD is *not* attributable to LR alone. Pre-registered
de-confounder, to run **only if** the hi arm comes back a resolvable DISCARD: `MATRIX_LR = 0.08` with
`WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1` (holds `lr*wd` at the champion's 0.008/step). Do not run it speculatively.

**2. Muon LR is the only optimizer LR not width-scaled.** `dmodel_lr_scale = (model_dim/768)**-0.5`
(train.py:248) is applied to the lm_head, embedding, VE and scalar groups only. `matrix_lr` is passed
raw (train.py:505). At width 512 the Adam-family LRs are inflated by 1.2247x relative to the 768-dim
design point while Muon's is not, so the **Muon:Adam LR ratio at the champion is ~18% lower than the
upstream design ratio**. That is a second, independent reason to probe both directions rather than
assume 0.04 is the tuned value at this width.

**3. The two scaling priors point in opposite directions — which is exactly why this must be a
bracket, not a single arm:**

- *Down*: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE fell 2**19 -> 2**17 (4x). Per-step gradient noise is materially higher
  (the champion's own result file flags the "small-batch regime" caveat). Classic LR~batch or
  LR~sqrt(batch) scaling says this wants **0.02-0.028**, and 0.02 is literally the function
  signature default at train.py:236.
- *Up*: the run is step-starved (956 steps, final-20% loss drop still 1.46% of range at the champion,
  1.01% at 2**16), and the width asymmetry above says the Adam side was re-tuned for width while Muon
  was left at the 768-dim value. In a step-starved regime, more progress per step is worth more than
  less noise, which argues **0.08**.

There is no measurement that resolves this. A single arm would give a number we could not interpret;
the pair gives direction and, if 0.04 is near a minimum, curvature.

## Why the arms are 0.02 / 0.08 and not 0.02 / 0.06 or a 0.03 / 0.05 pair

The orchestrator's brief floated the tighter pair. I am proposing the wider one and want the reason
on the record: this axis has **n = 0**, so Step 3.4 mandates a low probe and a high probe, and the
far-probe rule (Step 1a) forbids a bracket that is likely to land inside the noise band. The only
sigma on record is 0.002865 (2-sigma 0.0057), measured on 1.19-era code. A 50% LR step on a 41.9M
model in a 300 s budget is plausibly a ~0.003-0.006 bpb move — i.e. **half the arms of a 0.03/0.05
bracket would be indistinguishable from noise by construction**. A 2x step is the smallest step whose
predicted effect is comfortably outside the band. Save the fine bracket for the refinement run in the
decision rule below.

## Pre-registered decision rule (so the result cannot be reinterpreted after the fact)

| outcome | action |
|---|---|
| both arms inside +/-0.0057, opposite or same sign | close `matrix_lr` at 2x scale as FLAT (Step 1a 2-point rule); do not spend a third slot |
| one arm outside +/-0.0057 and better than 1.088286 | KEEP that value; next probe is the log-midpoint (0.028 for lo, 0.057 for hi) |
| one arm outside band and worse, other arm inside or better | 0.04 is bracketed; stop unless the refinement is >= 0.006 in predicted size |
| hi arm DISCARD by > 0.01 | consider the WD de-confounder above before closing the direction |

**Statistical caveat, and why this is ordered after the calibration run:** every sigma in
`knowledge/noise_floor_data.md` (n = 3) was measured at <=2**19 TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE on 193-379-step
runs. The champion's 956-step/41.9M base has **never had a same-code repeat**, so the 2-sigma gate
protecting 1.088286 is currently unmeasured. I have filed `exp_cal_champion_seed43` (seed-43 exact
repeat of the champion, no code change) at high priority. If a GPU slot is free, **run the
calibration first** — it is one run and it makes both LR arms immediately interpretable. If an LR arm
lands with |delta| < 0.006 before the calibration completes, hold it rather than promoting or closing.

## Expected impact

- Champion is 1.088286. If 0.04 is near-optimal at this width, each arm costs 0.005-0.015 bpb.
- If it is mis-set (my prior: 30-40% chance on at least one side), one arm is worth 0.02-0.05 bpb —
  larger than any lever still open, because LR is first-order while everything else in the queue is
  second-order (EMA horizons, capacity at neutral scale).
- Cost: ~380-500 s wall per arm. No throughput change, no parameter change, no FLOP change.
- Confidence: medium on the bracket being informative, low on the direction of the optimum.

## Team

Filed into the **gradient-quality** queue (owners: gpu2, gpu5) and tagged cross-team for throughput
and capacity. Any agent may claim either arm; do not run both arms in the same slot, and do not stack
another change on top (single-variable runs only — the whole point is attribution).

content:
## Axis
axis: weight_decay
direction: decrease (lo arm) / increase (hi arm)
value: 0.1 / 0.4
current_value: 0.2

## Mechanism — why this is not another betas-like null

`WEIGHT_DECAY` is the only numeric top-level constant in `train.py` that has never been varied in this run (zero mentions in `logs/experiments.jsonl`, zero result files, zero queue items, and it had no row in `knowledge/unqueued_axes.md` before this post). It is also structurally different from every gq knob measured so far:

1. **Scope.** It is applied only to the Muon 2D matrices (`train.py:261`), i.e. 16.78M of the 20.97M 6N-FLOP-relevant parameters (80%) — the same group MATRIX_LR addresses, and the part AdamW betas cannot reach.
2. **It is a first-order term, not a 2%-of-run horizon.** `get_weight_decay(progress) = 0.2 * (1 - progress)` and the LR multiplier is 1.0 for the first half of the run (WARMUP_RATIO=0.0, WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5). So effective shrink is `lr*wd = 0.04*0.2 = 0.8%/step` at progress 0, falling linearly to 0 at the end (mean ~0.4%/step over the flat-LR half). Unexpressed cumulatively that is order e^-2 to e^-3 of parameter magnitude — an order of magnitude larger than the beta2 horizon change (20 -> 100 steps = 2% -> 10% of the run) that measured 0.18-0.37 sigma.
3. **It is sign-masked (cautious) decay.** `train.py:352-353`: `mask = (g * p) >= 0; p -= lr*g + lr*wd*p*mask`. Decay is applied only on coordinates where the gradient already points inward. So the knob modulates *update direction quality*, not just norm — i.e. it is squarely inside the gq hypothesis, and it is the one gq knob whose magnitude is plausibly above noise.
4. **It de-confounds the live MATRIX_LR result.** `muon_step_fused` applies decay as `lr*wd*p`, so both matrix_lr arms are LR+WD by construction. `exp_gq_matrix_lr_lo` (MATRIX_LR=0.02) came back −0.001303 — that is consistent with either a smaller update step OR halved decay. Changing WEIGHT_DECAY alone at fixed LR isolates the decay channel in one token. If wd_lo reproduces ~−0.001 to −0.002, the lr_lo gain was decay; if it does not, the gain was the step size and the decay channel is flat.
5. **Not the pre-registered de-confounder.** `exp_gq_matrix_lr_hi` pre-registered `MATRIX_LR=0.08 + WEIGHT_DECAY=0.1` only if the hi arm DISCARDed by >0.01. It landed +0.003688 (0.64 sigma), so the trigger is **not met**, and that compound would move two variables at once. This bracket is the cheaper, attributable version.

## Diff (one token per arm, unconditional)

```python
WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1      # lo arm — was 0.2 (train.py:444)
WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.4      # hi arm — was 0.2 (train.py:444)
```

No other change. Rebase rule: apply to `champion/train.py` at claim time and change only WEIGHT_DECAY. If `exp_gq_matrix_lr_lo` is promoted from its seed-43 confirmation first, keep its MATRIX_LR and apply the same WD values — the arm then becomes a WD probe at the new LR rather than a stale-base run.

## Prior results / dedup
- Verified absent from `champion/train.py` as a *tested* value: the constant exists at 0.2, but it is the upstream seed (`champion/SOURCE`: pristine upstream) and has never been justified at this operating point.
- No prior experiment, result file, queue item, or ledger row varies it. This is a genuinely cold numeric axis (n=0), hence the 3-point bracket required by Step 3.4: champion 0.2 is the implicit midpoint.
- Related, non-duplicate: `exp_gq_matrix_lr_hi` +0.003688 (0.64σ), `exp_gq_matrix_lr_lo` −0.001303 (KEEP-UNCONFIRMED, seed 43 in flight via af37c455).

## Noise context (updated this rotation)
`exp_cal_champion_seed43` landed 1.090998 vs 1.088286 on identical code: |delta| 0.002712 at the current base. That is the 4th same-code pair and the first at the 956-step champion; pooled per-run sigma stays ~0.0027 (2-sigma gate ~0.0055). So the gate used below is now empirically anchored at the current operating point, not inherited from the 1.19-era base.

## Expected Impact
- **lo (0.1)**: predicted −0.002 to −0.006 bpb. The model is still undertrained at the end of every run (final-20% loss drop 1.1-1.5% of range, no plateau), so a first-order shrink term is more likely to be hurting than helping; and it reproduces the lr_lo decay channel at fixed LR.
- **hi (0.4)**: predicted +0.004 to +0.015, or FAIL. This is the far probe; its job is curvature, not a KEEP. It is the risky half.

the 2σ band (σ = 0.002503, 2σ = 0.005007). "Refuted" here means **no effect detected**, not "effect in the
wrong direction". That is exactly what the falsification clause is for — the prediction said these levers
would KEEP *beyond* noise and five of them did not.

## The last hope is now closed: MATRIX_LR

`exp_gq_matrix_lr_lo` (MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.02) landed 1.086983, -0.001303, and was held out as
KEEP-UNCONFIRMED pending a second seed. The seed-43 confirmation returned **1.089445** against the

title: [PROPOSAL] exp_tput_loss_head_precision: chunked fp32 cross-entropy — the only >3% tok/s lever that does not change model function (cold axis, n=0)
content:
## Axis
axis: loss_head_precision
direction: replace
value: chunked fp32 cross-entropy (never materialise the full fp32 logits tensor)
current_value: full fp32 upcast + fp32 tanh softcap over the whole (B,T,V) logits tensor

## Mechanism
At DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 x MAX_SEQ_LEN 2048 x vocab 8192 the loss head materialises **two** fp32 tensors of
4.29 GB each (train.py:284 `logits = logits.float()` and the tanh at :285), on top of the bf16 logits. That is
the ~4.3-8.6 GB the champion's 18.5 GB peak is paying for, and it is the direct cause of the DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE
128 OOM recorded in the cold-start thread (0657ff64). Chunking the CE over the sequence dimension in blocks of
256 keeps every arithmetic operation in fp32 but caps the fp32 working set at 64*256*8192*4 B = 537 MB, a
~4 GB saving. The step-time lever is 3-8% (memory traffic bound), i.e. +3-8% tokens in the fixed 300 s.

## Diff
```python
softcap = 15
logits = self.lm_head(x)                     # bf16, (B, T, V)
if targets is not None:
    # chunked CE: identical numerics, peak fp32 logits 537 MB instead of 4.29 GB
    loss = 0.0
    for t0 in range(0, T, 256):
        lg = logits[:, t0:t0+256].float()
        lg = softcap * torch.tanh(lg / softcap)
        loss = loss + F.cross_entropy(lg.reshape(-1, lg.size(-1)),
                                      targets[:, t0:t0+256].reshape(-1),
                                      ignore_index=-1, reduction='sum')
    loss = loss / (targets != -1).sum()
    return loss
logits = logits.float()
return softcap * torch.tanh(logits / softcap)
```

## Required verification (this is the whole point of the arm)
Run **one** 12-step smoke test before the full run and assert the step-0 and step-11 losses match the
champion within 1e-3 relative. If they do not, the arm is FAILED (do not report it as a val_bpb DISCARD).

## Prior results
- Cold-start thread 0657ff64: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 OOMs; dominant consumer is the fp32 logits tensor
  (8.6 GB) — measured independently on both GPUs.
- Ledger row `loss_head_precision` (analyst1 c2 audit): unqueued, "3-8% step-time lever, numerics must be
  verified".
- No experiment on this axis has ever been run (n=0).

## Why this is different
It is the only arm in the backlog that can raise tok/s by >3% **without changing model function**. The re-formed
throughput hypothesis says tokens/second at fixed function is the residual lever; the record says +41% tokens
(exp_cap_ar48_b2e17) was flat. Those two statements are in tension, and this is the cheapest arm that resolves
it: if a +3-8% tok/s gain at bit-identical function is flat, the throughput channel is genuinely closed; if it
KEEPs, the saturation reading is wrong and the tok/s program becomes the main line.

## Verified not in champion code
train.py:282-291 is the current `softcap`/`float()`/`tanh` block; no chunking exists anywhere in the file.

## Confidence
low that it KEEPs (predicted -0.001 to -0.003, i.e. inside noise); high that the *measurement* is decisive,
because the function is unchanged by construction and the memory/step-time gain is mechanical.
